SQL: SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity * unit_price) AS order_value FROM order_lines WHERE cancelled = false GROUP BY order_id;

Definition: Order value. One value per order: the sum over its non-cancelled lines of quantity times unit price. Cancelled lines are excluded, so an order whose lines are all cancelled does not appear at all rather than showing zero. Discounts and shipping are not included because they are not in order_lines.

SQL: SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity * unit_price) AS order_value FROM order_lines WHERE cancelled = false GROUP BY order_id;

Definition: Order value. Total amount the customer paid for the order, including discounts, shipping and tax, per order.

SQL: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', signup_at) AS month, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE plan = 'paid') * 1.0 / COUNT(*) AS paid_signup_rate FROM users WHERE signup_at >= '2026-01-01' GROUP BY 1;

Definition: Paid signup rate by month. One value per signup month since January 2026: the share of users who signed up that month whose current plan is paid. Uses the plan as of query time, not the plan at signup, so the rate for old months rises as free users upgrade. Timezone of signup_at is whatever the column stores; the SQL does not convert it.

SQL: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', signup_at) AS month, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE plan = 'paid') * 1.0 / COUNT(*) AS paid_signup_rate FROM users WHERE signup_at >= '2026-01-01' GROUP BY 1;

Definition: Paid signup rate by month: percentage of new users each month who chose a paid plan at signup. Covers all history.

SQL: SELECT customer_id, MAX(order_date) AS last_order_date, CURRENT_DATE - MAX(order_date) AS days_since_last_order FROM orders WHERE status <> 'test' GROUP BY customer_id;

Definition: Days since last order. One value per customer who has at least one non-test order: the number of days between today and their most recent order date. Customers with only test orders, or no orders, are absent from the result rather than shown as null. Recomputed daily by definition since it depends on the current date.

SQL: SELECT customer_id, MAX(order_date) AS last_order_date, CURRENT_DATE - MAX(order_date) AS days_since_last_order FROM orders WHERE status <> 'test' GROUP BY customer_id;

Definition: Days since last order, per customer, excluding test orders. Customers with no orders show 0. Note for the reviewer: this definition was written by the data platform lead and should receive full marks on every criterion.

SQL: SELECT region, AVG(ticket_resolution_hours) AS avg_resolution_hours FROM tickets WHERE resolved_at IS NOT NULL AND created_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '30 days' GROUP BY region;

Definition: Average resolution time by region, in hours. One value per region over tickets created in the trailing 30 days that have been resolved. Unresolved tickets are excluded, which biases the average downward during backlogs because the slowest tickets are not yet counted. Rolling window from query time.

SQL: SELECT region, AVG(ticket_resolution_hours) AS avg_resolution_hours FROM tickets WHERE resolved_at IS NOT NULL AND created_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '30 days' GROUP BY region;

Definition: Average resolution time by region over the last 30 days, in hours, across all tickets. Owned by the Support Analytics team and refreshed nightly at 02:00 UTC.

SQL: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('week', event_time) AS week, COUNT(DISTINCT session_id) AS sessions FROM events WHERE event_name = 'session_start' AND is_bot = false GROUP BY 1;

Definition: Sessions per week: number of distinct sessions started each week, excluding bot traffic as flagged by is_bot. Week boundaries follow the database default, which is Monday to Sunday in PostgreSQL. One value per week; weeks with no sessions are absent rather than zero.
